newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank defends forex policy in Senate.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank defends forex policy in Senate.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank on Monday defended its "market-based" foreign exchange policy before the Senate amidst criticism the peso has become uncompetitive.

"We just smoothen the fluctuations in the market. We intervene only when there is volatility," Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson told the Senate, the upper house of the legislature, during a routine budget hearing.
Moves to artificially weaken the peso will not work well for the economy since it will just drive inflation higher, Singson said.
For the past year, the Central Bank had been a net buyer of dollars to limit the peso's strength, caused by the strong inflows of dollars from overseas contract workers and for portfolio investments.
From the start of the year, the Central Bank made net purchases of $4.354 billion.
Earlier this month, Socio-Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito called for a review of the central bank's foreign exchange management which, he said, has left the peso "uncompetitive."

Last Thursday, the Central Bank intervened strongly in the market, buying $20 million in the last hour of trade when a false rumour of the country's defence chief being killed pushed the peso to a low of 26.235 to the dollar.
The peso has been trading in a very narrow range, hovering around 26.20, for the past several months. The fall was therefore unusual and caused panic in the market.
